WITHIN rs that is now satisfied — whoami, send, report, inbox and the Telegram sidecar all resolve through the single `resolve_seat` authority and therefore cannot drift. The residual disagreement I originally hit is between the LEGACY `pij whoami` (which answers from the legacy store) and the rs-routed `pij send`; that split lives in the legacy router, outside this plan's fence and outside the Rust workspace. Naming it as a plan-130 obligation would be scope creep, so it goes to prime as a note: the two CLIs can still answer differently about who a seat is, and only a cross-CLI change can close that. | — | — | — | — |

| v5 | round-3 regression risk | confirmed | LOW, after probing the seams these commits actually disturbed rather than asserting it. (1) The riskiest structural change is that `SidecarAction::request` became async and now takes a `&DaemonClient`, so EVERY sidecar action routes through a function that can refuse on identity — but only the Telegram arm resolves. I probed the blast radius directly rather than reasoning about it: `sidecar chore-run --target &lt;path&gt;` with BOTH PIJ_SESSION_ID and TMUX_PANE unset still returns `ok — {"job_id":3,…}`, so the identity requirement did not leak onto the non-Telegram arms. (2) Telegram itself does now require a resolvable acting seat where it previously accepted any asserted `--from`; that is the intended posture and its reach is bounded — there is no in-repo caller of `pij-rs sidecar telegram` outside the CLI and its own tests, and the live operator channel runs the legacy `pij send pij-telegram` route, which these commits do not touch. The new paneless register guidance mitigates the one population (paneless seats) that now needs an id it might not have had. (3) I considered whether embedding the POSIX gesture `env -u PIJ_SESSION_ID` in a daemon response is a portability regression, given this repo runs a windows-compat sensor, and DISMISSED it on the logic: that branch fires only when an observable pane contradicts an asserted id, a pane implies tmux, and tmux implies a POSIX shell — so the advice is always executable wherever it can appear. (4) `register` success now carries meta where it previously carried none; no consumer asserts its absence and the TypeScript suite passes. (5) The whole of AC1-AC6 remains green under my own 593/593 run, so nothing round 2 confirmed was regressed by round 3. | — | — | — | — |
